hero.name: Dono Artyk
intro: I'm a DevOps engineer with 5+ years building AWS and Kubernetes platforms.

I work on the shared infrastructure layer — the part that lets application teams deploy, secure, observe, and operate their services without each one solving TLS, DNS, identity, and secrets on its own.

Lately most of my work has been agentic AI engineering with Claude Code and MCP: automated pull-request review, requirement traceability, and custom agent skills running across an organization's repositories.
I like systems that keep working when nobody is watching them.

bullets: Built Claude Code and MCP pull-request review automation across 30+ repositories and 400+ pull requests, catching missing requirements, security issues, and exposed secrets before human review.

Replaced ingress-nginx with Kubernetes Gateway API and AWS Load Balancer Controller across 5 application teams, cutting production traffic over through weighted Route 53 shifts and connection draining.
Owned cert-manager, external-dns, and Secrets Store CSI Driver on multi-tenant production EKS — automated DNS-01 certificate issuance and moved 8 services to IAM-scoped runtime secret mounts.
Built HA Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager for non-production, removing ~$31K/year in licensing spend, and set 99.9% SLOs with burn-rate alerting that cut page volume 45%.
Ran ArgoCD App-of-Apps and Helm delivery for 5 application teams, giving 20+ engineers Git-based releases, drift detection, and a repeatable rollback path.
Replatformed the infrastructure behind 40+ containerized EKS microservices from CloudFormation to reusable Terraform modules, with zero-downtime cluster and private-node cutovers.
Replaced static AWS credentials across 45+ GitHub Actions pipelines with short-lived, least-privilege IAM roles through OIDC federation.
Moved Lambda, API Gateway, and DynamoDB from AWS CDK to Terraform, bringing serverless resources under the same IaC workflow with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authentication.
Containerized a legacy Flask/MySQL production application and migrated its four services from Docker Compose to Kubernetes with EBS-backed persistent storage.
Automated AWS account provisioning across 35+ accounts with Control Tower and Service Control Policies, cutting environment setup from 3 days to under 2 hours.
Removed 10+ hours of weekly operational toil with Python/boto3 and Ansible automation for cross-account S3 lifecycle and patch-compliance workflows.
Brought unmanaged VPC networking, IAM deployment roles, and S3 infrastructure into Terraform modules and state, replacing manual cloud changes with repeatable IaC and drift detection.

projects.name: Agentic PR review platform
projects.problem: Teams adopting AI-assisted coding could suddenly write code far faster than senior engineers could review it. The bottleneck just moved downstream.
bullets: Automated first-pass review across 30+ repositories and 400+ pull requests, wired in as one reusable CI workflow instead of thirty separate copies.
Pulls the ticket's acceptance criteria alongside the diff, so the review catches missing requirements — not just style.
Advisory by design: the agent comments, and humans plus deterministic checks still decide what merges.

code.title: .github/workflows/pr-review.yml
lines: types: [opened, reopened]   # not on every push

projects.name: Shared Kubernetes platform layer
projects.problem: Every team on the cluster needed the same four things — a hostname, TLS, AWS access, and credentials — and each one was solving them by hand, differently.
bullets: Automated certificate issuance end to end with DNS-01 validation, so renewal stopped being something a person has to remember.
Gave every workload its own identity: an IAM role scoped to exactly one secret, and no static AWS keys anywhere in the cluster.
Eight workloads moved onto the standardized pattern — two as deep implementations, six as adoption once the pattern existed.

code.title: httproute.yaml - all an application team writes
lines: # DNS records, certificate issuance, the ACM import
# and the IAM role behind it are the platform's job.

projects.name: GitOps delivery for a streaming pipeline
projects.problem: A six-component streaming stack was deployed imperatively from CI — so CI held cluster credentials, ordering was guesswork, and a manual change to a live resource silently won.
bullets: Replaced push-based deploys with pull-based GitOps: the cluster reconciles toward Git, and CI never holds cluster credentials.
Dependency order is declared rather than timed — each stage waits on the previous one being genuinely healthy, not on a sleep.
Nothing sensitive in the repository; the database pulls its credentials at runtime through workload identity.

code.title: apps/kafka.yaml
lines: path: components/kafka  # git is the only way in
prune: true           # gone from git, gone here

stack.ai_line: Agentic AI is part of how I work day to day — Claude Code, MCP integrations, and custom agent skills wired into real engineering workflows, with human review kept authoritative.

about.heading: About me
paragraphs: I'm curious by nature and usually happiest when I'm figuring something out. I like problems where the answer isn't obvious and tend to keep pulling the thread until everything finally makes sense. I'm always looking for something new to learn, explore, or understand a little more deeply.

Outside of work, you'll usually find me hiking, doing yoga, planning my next trip, or experimenting with a new recipe. I love discovering new kinds of tea, and I'm always looking for a book that stays with me — The Choice by Edith Eger is one I keep coming back to.
I like being active, exploring new places, and keeping life interesting. I'm probably already thinking about what to learn, cook, read, or see next.
